title: Clatterhusk's Rattling Ranks
story: In the old Chalkstone Amphitheatre, Clatterhusk the Husk Captain drills a shimmering army of beetles in neat rows, rattling his wing-cases like a drum. Most of that army, Mr 6 notices, flickers strangely in the moonlight — husk-mirrors, not beetles at all. He lifts his silver horn and counts before he blows.
question: Clatterhusk marches 14 rows of 9 beetles. Only one third of them are real — the rest are hollow husk-mirrors that vanish at a sound. If each blast of Mr 6's silver horn sends 7 real beetles scuttling home, how many blasts does he need?
solution: The ranks hold 14 × 9 = 126 shapes in all.
One third are real beetles: 126 ÷ 3 = 42 real ones.
praise: Setting up rows × columns was exactly right — the step that slipped was thinning the army down to the one third that was actually real before dividing by 7.
hint: Count the whole formation first, then keep only the real third of it — those are the only beetles the horn has to move.
victory: Six blasts — one for each of him, Mr 6 joked — and 42 real beetles trotted home while 84 husk-mirrors popped like soap bubbles. Clatterhusk saluted the clever little numeral and marched off to drill nothing but echoes.
imagePrompt: A tall armored beetle captain rattling his wing-cases before shimmering moonlit ranks of beetles in a ruined chalk-white amphitheatre, with a caped numeral-6 knight raising a silver horn and counting rows.
